THIS FILE RECORDS DEFECTS, NOT EXPECTED ANSWERS. The expected answers live in the generator, taken
verbatim from the SPEC clauses they pin — this file only says 'this (row, engine, cell) is
known-broken today, here is why, and here is a hand fixture that reproduces it without the
generator'. If you find yourself editing an expected value into this file, stop: the oracle for
R1–R6 is the spec, and weakening it here would turn a differential into a description.
IT RATCHETS BOTH WAYS. A failing cell that is NOT listed here fails the suite. An entry listed here
whose cells ALL pass ALSO fails the suite, so a waiver cannot outlive its defect and start masking
the defect's return. Deleting the entry is part of the fix.
Every entry this file has carried was found by PART 27 on 2026-07-27, the first time it ran, and
then RE-DERIVED from a hand-written report + policy, so that no waiver rested on the generator
being right.

entry this file ever held (R5 `value-grammar`) was written `engine: "*"` because the ⟨0.24⟩ §6.2
`--class` VALUE GRAMMAR was found UNIMPLEMENTED IN ALL FOUR ENGINES — a shared gap, not a
divergence, which is the only shape a blanket waiver may take. It was narrowed to `ts` that same
evening as rust, swift and java landed their halves, and DELETED when candor-ts landed its half and
the ratchet reported it STALE. The waiver named its own exit condition, the fix met it, and the
entry went with it; its text is in this file's git history, not preserved in a comment here,
because a dead waiver kept 'for context' is exactly what the both-ways ratchet exists to prevent.
MEASURED AT DELETION (`python3 gen_rung024.py --only R5 --baseline rung024-baseline.json`): all
FOUR engines OK on all three R5 cells (dynamic, discriminates, value-grammar) — 12 live cells, no
unwaived failure and no stale waiver. An earlier run the same evening reported the java cells
ABSENT (the jar was mid-rebuild and not invocable), which is worth recording because it is exactly
the shape an unexplained measurement change takes on a box with several engines moving at once: the
ratchet reports what is ON THE BOX, so a java cell that regresses will fail UNWAIVED rather than
quietly reading as absent.

⟨0.24⟩ 2026-08-01 — FOUR R11 entries added the day the row was written. This is the intended shape for a
row that pins a RULING ahead of its implementations: the law is stated, the row measures it, all four
engines fail it, and each waiver names its own exit condition. The alternative — writing the row after
the engines comply — would have made it unfalsifiable at birth, which is how `coverage.modules` and the
policy-vocabulary field each reached three spellings before anyone noticed.

known.why: report envelope: java emits top-level `packages` (list) where the other three emit `package` (str), plus per-entry `entryPoint` and `fs` that no sibling carries. Pre-existing and byte-identical on the pre-round jar — R10 is reporting it, not causing it. FIX: adjudicate `package` vs `packages` in SPEC 2 (the envelope field is singular everywhere else in the document), then converge; decide separately whether entryPoint/fs are legitimate engine extensions or drift.

report envelope: rust carries none of `declared`/`undeclared`/`overdeclared`/`unresolved` that the other three emit per entry. Note the review measured a SEMANTIC divergence underneath this one that R10 cannot see (java `undeclared:["Exec","Fs","Net"]` vs ts/swift `undeclared:[]` for the SAME situation — opposite readings of 'no declaration'), so fixing the key set alone would produce agreement on shape over a disagreement on meaning. Settle the semantics FIRST.

R11 ⟨0.24⟩ ADVISORY-VERB CONFIDENCE LAW (SPEC §3.2, ruled `4fd140c`), not yet implemented in ANY engine. Over a report carrying `hosts` but no `netClass`, `gate --report` REFUSES on §3.1 answerability while `unverified` answers from a FALLBACK DERIVATION and clears the function — the advisory verb more confident than the gate over identical bytes. Measured four-way the day the row was written. NOTE THE HISTORY: a weaker form of this row (gate-not-clean => the verb names SOMETHING) passed on all four engines, because the verb names a DIFFERENT hole; only the per-function form catches it. FIX: `unverified` names the function the gate could not judge, with the MISSING EVIDENCE as the reason and never the derived class; `fix-gate` offers no remedy premised on evidence the gate refused to read; both carry the gate's `unevaluated` shape; `--strict` exits 2.
